questions.q: In its split verdict of January 2026 on Section 17A of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988, which one of the following correctly describes the stand of Justice K.V. Viswanathan?
o: He struck down the provision as a violation of Article 14
He upheld the provision exactly as enacted, leaving approval with the Government
He held the provision valid because Section 19 already protects officials at the prosecution stage
He upheld the provision, but only if the prior approval comes from a binding opinion of an independent authority such as the Lokpal or Lokayuktas
questions.e: Justice Viswanathan saved Section 17A only on a condition: approval to probe a public servant's official decisions must come from an independent body (Lokpal at the Centre, Lokayuktas in States). The Section 19 argument and the Article 14 reasoning belong to Justice Nagarathna, who struck the provision down. Because the two judges differed, the matter goes to the CJI for a larger bench.
questions.s: All India Radio News; Drishti IAS, 30 Jan 2026

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Supreme Court's January 2026 directions on police media briefings:
1. All States were asked to frame a policy on police media briefings within three months.
2. The policy is to be modelled on a manual prepared by amicus curiae Gopal Sankaranarayanan.
3. The 16 guidelines on police encounters were laid down in the Prakash Singh case.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Court gave States three months to frame media-briefing policies, using the amicus's manual as the model, in proceedings arising from PUCL petitions. The 16 encounter guidelines come from PUCL v. State of Maharashtra (2014), not the Prakash Singh police-reform case, so statement 3 is wrong.

questions.q:
The Supreme Court in January 2026 agreed to examine petitions by Tamil Nadu and Kerala on the Enforcement Directorate. Consider the following statements:
1. The question is whether the ED is a juristic person entitled to approach High Courts under Article 226.
2. The States contend that the ED has an express power to sue under the FEMA, 1999 and the PMLA, 2002.
3. Kerala's case concerned a State-appointed inquiry commission in a gold smuggling matter.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The States argue the opposite of statement 2: a statutory body holds only the powers expressly given to it, and neither FEMA nor PMLA gives the ED power to sue. Statements 1 and 3 are accurate; Tamil Nadu's own dispute concerned illegal mining.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Arbitration Council of India (ACI):
1. It is a statutory body provided for in Part IA (Sections 43A to 43M) of the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996.
2. It was provided for by the Arbitration and Conciliation (Amendment) Act, 2019, on the basis of the Justice B.N. Srikrishna Committee.
3. It has been functioning since 2019 and has framed grading norms for arbitral institutions.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The 2019 amendment inserted Part IA, creating the ACI on the Srikrishna Committee (2017) recommendation. The petition in the Supreme Court exists precisely because the Council has still not been constituted, so statement 3 is wrong.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding State of Uttar Pradesh v. Anurudh (2026):
1. The Supreme Court flagged the growing use of the POCSO Act, 2012 in consensual adolescent relationships.
2. The age of consent under POCSO and Section 63 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 is 16 years.
3. Section 19 of POCSO makes reporting of offences mandatory.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Court urged the Union government to consider corrective measures because criminal law is being applied to teenagers in consensual relationships. The age of consent is 18, not 16, under both POCSO and BNS Section 63, which is why such cases arise at all; Section 19 mandatory reporting adds to the problem.
questions.h: Eighteen, not sixteen, is the legal line

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about District Mineral Foundations (DMFs), on which the Allahabad High Court ruled in January 2026:
1. DMFs are statutory non-profit trusts under Section 9B of the MMDR Act, 1957.
2. Holders of leases granted before 12 January 2015 pay 10 per cent of royalty, and later leases pay 30 per cent.
3. Funds are spent under the Pradhan Mantri Khanij Kshetra Kalyan Yojana, with at least 60 per cent for high-priority areas.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Allahabad High Court treated the DMF law as beneficial legislation, to be read liberally for people hurt by mining. The royalty rates are the other way round: 30 per cent for pre-2015 leases and 10 per cent for later ones, so only statements 1 and 3 are correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the UGC (Promotion of Equity in Higher Education Institutions) Regulations, 2026:
1. They replaced the 2012 equity framework of the UGC.
2. Every higher education institution must set up an Equal Opportunity Centre and an Equity Committee.
3. The Equity Committee must report within 7 days of a complaint, and the institution head must act within 15 days.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The 2026 Regulations replaced the 2012 framework and make an Equal Opportunity Centre and Equity Committee compulsory in every institution. The time limits are muddled in statement 3: the Committee must meet within 24 hours and report within 15 days, and the head must act within 7 days.

questions.q: After the Supreme Court bench led by CJI Surya Kant stayed the UGC (Promotion of Equity in Higher Education Institutions) Regulations, 2026 on 29 January 2026, which framework continues to operate until further orders?
o: The 2026 Regulations, subject to the Court's modifications
An interim code to be framed by a committee of eminent jurists
No equity framework, as the Court left the field vacant
questions.e: The bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justice Joymalya Bagchi found the 2026 rules prima facie vague and open to misuse, and used Article 142 to keep the 2012 Regulations alive. The Court only suggested that a committee of eminent jurists revisit the rules; it did not frame an interim code.
questions.h: Stay the new, revive the old

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Supreme Court's January 2026 ruling on menstrual health in schools:
1. It held that menstrual health and hygiene management in schools form part of the right to life and dignity under Article 21.
2. The petition was filed by Dr. Jaya Thakur.
3. The Court treated it only as a policy goal under Article 47 that cannot be enforced.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Court tied menstrual hygiene to Article 21 and directed States and UTs to ensure functional gender-segregated toilets, free sanitary napkins through vending machines and MHM corners in every school. Treating it as an unenforceable Article 47 goal is the opposite of its reasoning.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Governor's address to a State legislature:
1. Article 176 requires the Governor to address the legislature at the start of the first session of each year.
2. The address is prepared by the State Council of Ministers and reflects the government's policy.
3. Under Article 175, the Governor must address the House at the start of every session.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Article 176 makes the address mandatory at the first session after a general election and the first session of each year, and it is drafted by the elected government, as the Nabam Rebia (2016) and Shamsher Singh (1974) line of cases says. Article 175 is optional: the Governor 'may' address the House, so statement 3 is wrong. The issue arose when Tamil Nadu's Governor walked out and Kerala's omitted paragraphs.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Governor's Rule in the Chakma Autonomous District Council in Mizoram:
1. The Governor extended it by six months with the support of the State Cabinet.
2. It was first imposed in July 2025.
3. Autonomous district councils have up to 30 members, of whom 26 are elected and up to four nominated.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The extension went ahead despite opposition from the State Cabinet, so statement 1 fails. The Chakma ADC was set up in 1972 under the Sixth Schedule, whose councils have up to 30 members (26 elected, up to 4 nominated) serving five-year terms; the Bodoland Territorial Council, with 46 members, is the exception.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Malayalam Language Bill, 2025 passed by the Kerala Legislative Assembly:
1. It makes Malayalam the compulsory first language in government and aided schools of the State.
2. A Bill of this kind may be reserved by the Governor for the consideration of the President under Article 200.
3. The State's earlier 2015 language Bill received the President's assent without any objection.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The 2025 Bill makes Malayalam the compulsory first language in government and aided schools, with minority students allowed to continue their mother tongue. Article 200 lets a Governor reserve a Bill for the President. The 2015 Bill was reserved and assent was withheld over conflict with the Official Languages Act, 1963, minority protection, the three-language formula and the RTE Act, so statement 3 is wrong.

questions.q:
Himachal Pradesh attained statehood in 1971 as the 18th State of the Union. Arrange the following stages of its constitutional status in chronological order:
1. Part C State
2. Chief Commissioner's Province
3. Union Territory
4. State
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
questions.e: Himachal was a Chief Commissioner's Province from 15 April 1948, became a Part C State in 1950, a Union Territory on 1 November 1956 and a full State on 25 January 1971 under the State of Himachal Pradesh Act, 1970. Statehood therefore came last, after UT status.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the 28th Conference of Speakers and Presiding Officers of the Commonwealth (CSPOC), held in January 2026:
1. It was inaugurated by the Prime Minister in the Central Hall of Samvidhan Sadan, New Delhi.
2. India had earlier hosted the conference in 1971, 1986 and 2010.
3. CSPOC was created in 1969 on the initiative of an Indian Speaker, and its secretariat is provided by India.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: PM Modi inaugurated the 28th CSPOC on 15 January 2026 with Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla in the chair, and India had hosted it in 1971, 1986 and 2010. CSPOC was founded in 1969 on the initiative of Canadian Speaker Lucien Lamoureux and Canada provides the secretariat, so statement 3 is wrong.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Budget Session of Parliament in 2026:
1. It began on 28 January 2026 and continued until 18 April 2026.
2. The Jan Vishwas (Amendment of Provisions) Bill, 2026 was among the Government Bills passed.
3. Only the Finance Bill was passed, and no Appropriation Bill was taken up.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The session ran from 28 January to 18 April 2026 and passed nine Government Bills, including the Finance Bill, 2026 and two Appropriation Bills, along with the Jan Vishwas (Amendment of Provisions) Bill, 2026. Statement 3 is wrong because Appropriation Bills must also pass for money to be drawn from the Consolidated Fund.

questions.q: ECINET, launched during the first India International Conference on Democracy and Election Management (IICDEM 2026) in January 2026, is best described as
o: a blockchain-based system for remote voting by migrant workers
a tracking system for the movement of electronic voting machines
a single platform integrating over 40 apps of the Election Commission of India
a helpline for voters who need to register complaints against candidates
questions.e: IICDEM 2026 was held at Bharat Mandapam from 21 January 2026, organised by the India International Institute of Democracy and Election Management (IIIDEM, set up in 2011, based in Dwarka). ECINET brings over 40 separate ECI apps into one platform, and the Delhi Declaration 2026 was adopted at the conference.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about delimitation in India:
1. Articles 82 and 170 provide for readjustment of Lok Sabha and State Assembly constituencies.
2. Orders of the Delimitation Commission can be modified by the House of the People if it finds them unfair.
3. The Commission that finalised J&K's constituencies in 2022 created 90 Assembly seats, 43 in Jammu and 47 in Kashmir.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Articles 82 and 170 govern readjustment, and the J&K exercise produced 90 Assembly seats (43 Jammu, 47 Kashmir). Orders of the Commission have the force of law and neither the House of the People nor a State Assembly may modify them; they take effect on a date notified by the President. Courts can review only manifestly arbitrary orders (Kishorchandra Chhanganlal Rathod, 2024).

questions.q: Nitin Nabin, elected national president of the Bharatiya Janata Party on 20 January 2026, is notable because he
o: became the youngest national president in the party's history
was earlier the party's national general secretary in charge of Bihar
was a sitting Union Cabinet Minister at the time of his election
previously served as Bihar Chief Minister
questions.e: Nabin was the BJP's working president and a Bihar minister from Bankipur before being elected on 20 January 2026 as the youngest national president. He had earlier led the Bharatiya Janata Yuva Morcha in Bihar; he was never Bihar's Chief Minister. The result was announced by national returning officer Dr K. Laxman at party headquarters during Sangathan Parv.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Central Vigilance Commission (CVC), to which Shri Praveen Vashista was appointed Vigilance Commissioner in January 2026:
1. It was set up in 1964 on the recommendation of the Santhanam Committee.
2. It got statutory status in 1964 itself.
3. Appointments are made on the recommendation of a committee of the Prime Minister, the Union Home Minister and the Leader of Opposition in Lok Sabha.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The CVC began in 1964 on the Santhanam Committee's advice, but it received statutory status only through the CVC Act, 2003, so statement 2 is wrong. Appointments under Section 4(1) follow the recommendation of the three-member committee, with a tenure of four years or age 65.

questions.q:
On the Lokpal Foundation Day, 16 January, consider the following statements:
1. It commemorates Section 3 of the Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act, 2013 coming into force on 16 January 2014.
2. The Lokpal has a Chairperson and up to eight members, all of whom must be judicial members.
3. The Selection Committee includes the Prime Minister, the Speaker, the Leader of Opposition, the CJI or a nominee, and an eminent jurist.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: At least 50 per cent of Lokpal members must be judicial members, not all of them, so statement 2 is wrong. The other two statements are accurate. Maharashtra set up the first Lokayukta in 1971.

questions.q: The National Dam Safety Authority (NDSA) issued a show-cause notice to the Narmada Valley Development Authority in January 2026 over safety concerns at which dam?
o: Indira Sagar Dam, on the Narmada River in Madhya Pradesh
Tehri Dam, on the Bhagirathi River in Uttarakhand
Sardar Sarovar Dam, on the Narmada River in Gujarat
Bargi Dam, on the Narmada River in Madhya Pradesh
questions.e: The NDSA, a statutory body under the Dam Safety Act, 2021 with headquarters in New Delhi, acted over Bargi Dam, a multipurpose dam built between 1974 and 1990 on the Narmada in Madhya Pradesh. The other dams are real Narmada or Himalayan projects but were not the subject of the notice.

questions.q:
Following the contaminated tap-water outbreak in Indore in January 2026, consider the following statements about urban water governance in India:
1. Water supply is a State subject, and the 74th Constitutional Amendment widened the role of municipalities in it.
2. Drinking water quality standards are specified by the Bureau of Indian Standards in IS 10500.
3. AMRUT 2.0 is administered by the Ministry of Jal Shakti.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Water supply sits in the State sphere and urban local bodies run it after the 74th Amendment; BIS sets the drinking-water norms in IS 10500. AMRUT and AMRUT 2.0 belong to the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs, which also runs the Pey Jal Survekshan, so statement 3 is wrong. The NHRC took suo motu notice after a main pipeline was found passing beneath a public toilet.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about PRAGATI, whose 50th meeting was held in January 2026:
1. It is a technology-enabled platform launched in 2015 for reviewing projects and grievances, with review meetings chaired by the Prime Minister.
2. It hosts governance tools such as PM Gati Shakti and PARIVESH.
3. Its review meetings are chaired by the Cabinet Secretary.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: PRAGATI (Pro-Active Governance and Timely Implementation) was launched in 2015 and its review meetings are chaired by the Prime Minister, directly engaging Union ministries and States. It hosts PM Gati Shakti and PARIVESH. An Oxford Said Business School study called it a global benchmark; about 94 per cent of issues flagged have been resolved.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Land Stack, launched by the Ministry of Rural Development in January 2026:
1. It is a GIS-based integrated digital platform for land records.
2. It was launched in pilot locations Chandigarh and Tamil Nadu.
3. It functions under the Digital India Land Records Modernisation Programme (DILRMP).
4. It was launched by the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Land Stack is a GIS-based platform under DILRMP, piloted in Chandigarh and Tamil Nadu, and launched by the Ministry of Rural Development together with a Glossary of Revenue Terms. Statement 4 names the wrong ministry. Three statements are correct.

questions.q: The Ministry of Home Affairs has notified the 16th Census (Census 2027). For Phase II (population enumeration) in areas that are not snow-bound, the reference date is
questions.e: Phase II counts the population with a reference date of 1 March 2027. The date 1 October 2026 is the reference date used for snow-bound areas of Ladakh, Jammu and Kashmir, Himachal Pradesh and Uttarakhand. Phase I (house-listing) runs from 1 April to 30 September 2026.
questions.h: March for the many, October for the snow
